That covered the writers only: the census measures 63 hand-typed spellings of the same keys across the readers (34 inside the seven lanes that have or get an owner), and every raw SQL predicate was hand-typed, so renaming a key moved the writers and left the readers matching nothing - or, for the transfer gate's IS NULL arm, matching everything. Cluster #50 also left a note claiming GeneratePayoutBatchJob records a selected: 0 summary when it selects nothing; the shipped guard is if ($summary['selected'] > 0), and the gate now shows a zero run writes no audit row and dispatches nothing at all.
superseded_facts.now: Each bound lane key is spelled exactly once, by its owner; readers reach it through the constant or through MetadataLane, whose emitted SQL is frozen to the pre-fix text (19 predicates). The owner-less lanes keep 29 hand-typed spellings, pinned as a ceiling and named in the gate's docblock rather than hidden. The canonical full-suite run for this state is 5 skipped, 2939 passed (118730 assertions) in 598.35s with 0 failure markers (logs/suite51-final.txt); the sweep taken before this record was patched read 4 skipped, 2940 passed (118725 assertions), and the difference is named in the evidence block.

audit_subject_refused_at_the_door.statement: AuditLog::creating rejects the three subject shapes this codebase used to write (a lane label instead of a class, 0 instead of a key, one column without the other), so no writer can drift back into them unnoticed; the rejection is one hook, which is what makes 133 write sites enforceable.
audit_subject_refused_at_the_door.verification_note: 2 because the guard is both declared and called from booted(); deleting either half is the regression this claim is written to see.

no_writer_invents_an_audit_subject.statement: No writer in app/, config/ or routes/ puts a quoted label into auditable_type any more: the fourteen run-row sites across twelve files name a null subject and carry their lane in metadata.lane, which is where the house filters already look.

audit_subject_contract_is_gated.statement: The subject contract is enforced by a test file that writes rows, reads them back through the eager loader and the admin table formatter, and runs the settlement listener twice to prove its dedupe filter works, rather than being restated in prose.

no_hand_spelled_anchor_json_path.statement: No file in app/ spells the anchor's json address by hand any more: the two acceptable path arms are built from AuditLog::ANCHOR_KEY and AuditLog::LEGACY_ANCHOR_KEY inside scopeAnchoredBy, so a writer and a reader cannot disagree about the key of the same column without one of them naming the constant that no longer exists. Before this, `metadata->audit_anchor` was written in sixteen files and `metadata->anchor` in five, including one raw json_extract, and each file was internally consistent.
no_hand_spelled_anchor_json_path.verification_note: The model is exempt by construction: it concatenates the paths from the constants, so the literal string never appears there either, which is exactly the point of the claim.

legacy_anchor_spelling_is_read_only.statement: Rows written before the rename are still found and still dedupe: the desk filter and every guard accept the old `anchor` key through an OR arm, while no writer is allowed to produce it. That is what makes the fix safe on an append-only table with no backfill (backfilling audit_logs is refused by the retention policy).

audit_anchor_contract_is_gated.statement: The anchor contract is enforced by tests/Feature/Audit/AuditAnchorTruthTest.php, which drives the withdrawal KYC listener and the prize disbursement scribe through their real entry points and then asks the admin search for the row by its anchor (0 hits before the fix, 1 after), proves a pre-rename row is still findable and still dedupes its lane, and names by file the four app/ places allowed to carry an `anchor` key that is a payload field rather than audit metadata.

no_hand_spelled_referral_clause_outside_.statement: Attributed players are selected in one place in app/: Agent::referredPlayersQuery(), whose whereJsonContains on preferences->referred_by_agent_id is the only such line in the application. Before this, the report service and both agent portal surfaces (the referrals list and a referral detail) each carried their own hand-written copy, so the number an agent was shown and the rows they were shown could come from four different queries. What was wrong was never the clause - cluster #48 measured that it compiles to correct SQL on both grammars - it was having four of them.
no_hand_spelled_referral_clause_outside_.verification_note: The model is exempt because it is the owner the pattern is looking for; one copy in any of the three directories makes this claim false, and the Infra test says so.

no_surface_displays_the_cached_referral_.statement: agents.total_referrals is written and never displayed: no file under app/Http, app/Services or app/Filament reads the property, and no Blade view mentions it, so every agent-facing and admin-facing figure is Agent::referredPlayerCount(). Measured before the change: with one of two attributed members removed the column said 2 while the rows said 1, and the agent portal printed both numbers on one screen - the strip showing the cache, the report card showing the count.
no_surface_displays_the_cached_referral_.verification_note: The only file in app/ allowed to touch the property is app/Models/Agent.php, which owns the recount; it is outside the directories searched because a cache needs a writer.

agent_referral_count_contract_is_gated.statement: tests/Feature/Agent/AgentReferralCountTruthTest.php holds the contract: the attribution writes a count and not an increment (its query log contains a COUNT against users and never an arithmetic update of the column), a moved player is counted by the agent who has her and given back by the one who lost her, the rendered portal page prints one number while the cache is deliberately drifted to 5, the report headline equals the size of the id set the report filters on, a recount writes nothing when the cache agrees and exactly one UPDATE when it does not, and the clause has one owner. Nine tests, 43 assertions; every rule was shown to hold by undoing it - 11 plants, 11 red, recorded in /home/user/logs/red49.txt.

operational_report_filters_narrow_rows.statement: tests/Feature/Operations/OperationalReportFilterTruthTest.php holds the contract: every key the desk advertises is consulted by the reader that receives it, is applied to a column, relation or metadata lane that this tree really has, and changes the rows on a seed where both outcomes exist. 14 tests, 155 assertions. The pre-fix behaviour was re-created and measured (29 keys advertised, 14 never consulted, filtering THB returning all 2 rows), and every rule was shown to hold by undoing it - 11 plants, 11 red, recorded in /home/user/logs/red50.txt.

no_report_filter_matches_every_row.statement: The one filter that was worse than ignored - `financial.user_id`, compiled to `wallet_id LIKE '%%'`, which returned 2 rows for a player who owned 1 - is gone: no where-clause in app/ filters a column with a bare LIKE of wildcards, and the user filter travels through the entry's wallet instead. The gate re-measures both.

failed_report_generation_persists.statement: A report generation that refuses seats Failed with its reason. It used to throw from inside the same DB::transaction that wrote the Failed row, so the write rolled back and the job returned to Queued forever with failure_reason null - the desk had no visible failure state at all. The refusal is now raised after the commit (one `throw $refusal;` outside the transaction callback, asserted by the gate).

bound_lane_keys_never_appear_in_raw_sql.statement: No metadata predicate in app/ or routes/ spells a bound lane key by hand: 34 such sites existed before cluster #51 and 0 exist now, measured by one rule applied to both trees (the "after" tree with tools/patch51code.py run in reverse, not a remembered count). Readers build the path through App\Support\Database\MetadataLane instead, used 19 times across 8 app/ files, and the text it emits is frozen against the pre-fix literals by 19 pairs in the gate, because rows already stored were written against those exact paths.

bound_lane_keys_never_appear_in_array_re.statement: The same rule holds for PHP array reads: no file reaches a bound lane with $metadata['claim'] or its seven siblings. 34 hand-typed spellings sat in 13 files before the fix (the claim lane alone accounted for 19 of them, and its owner had no constant at all); every one now goes through the owning class constant, so a rename cannot leave a reader behind. 29 spellings remain in lanes that have no single owner and are pinned as a ceiling of 29 in the gate rather than left uncounted.

metadata_lane_contract_is_gated.statement: tests/Feature/Payment/MetadataLaneTruthTest.php holds 8 tests: reachability of every bound lane predicate against rows the shipped writers produce, the census of hand-typed spellings, the frozen predicate text, and the zero-selection audit behaviour that cluster #50 recorded wrongly. Six planted regressions in logs/proof51red.txt each turn exactly the predicted test red.
